results.markdown:
Title: HVAC Advertising: Getting More Service Calls (2026)

URL Source: https://adwave.com/resources/hvac-advertising-getting-more-service-calls

Published Time: 2026-10-05T00:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
Trucks and reviews can look fine and the phone still stay quiet. Competitors take shoulder-season jobs while the schedule has gaps.

Most HVAC companies rely on one or two advertising channels and wonder why growth stalls. Google Ads capture people who are already searching. Yard signs work when you're already in the neighborhood. But neither builds the kind of sustained awareness that turns your company into the first name homeowners think of when the furnace dies at 11 p.m. on a Saturday.

The HVAC industry in the U.S. generates roughly [$31 billion in annual revenue](https://www.ibisworld.com/united-states/market-research-reports/hvac-services-industry/), and that number keeps climbing as aging housing stock and extreme weather push demand higher. But more demand also means more competition. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects [6% job growth for HVAC mechanics](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/installation-maintenance-and-repair/heating-air-conditioning-and-refrigeration-mechanics-and-installers.htm) through 2032, which translates to more companies fighting for the same homeowners.

This guide uses three words on purpose:

*   **Channel** is where the ad runs (Google, Facebook, a postcard, streaming TV).

*   **Inquiry** is a call, form, or message. A lead fee is a cost per inquiry. It is not a job on the board.

*   **Booked job** is an appointment or install you schedule after that inquiry. This page does not publish a booked-job rate, a close rate, or a return for any channel.

The sections below cover six channels, what each one is for, and what you pay for the inquiry when a source says so. For a wider channel list that also includes radio, yard signs, and referrals, see [best advertising for HVAC companies](https://adwave.com/resources/best-advertising-hvac-companies/). For how an Adwave campaign is set up, see [HVAC advertising on Adwave](https://adwave.com/hvac/). Those are separate pages. This one stays on inquiries.

## Google Ads and Local Services Ads

When a homeowner's air conditioner stops cooling in the middle of July, they don't scroll Instagram. They grab their phone and search "AC repair near me" or "emergency HVAC service." Google Ads put you at the top of those results, right when purchase intent is at its peak.

But for HVAC companies, standard Google Ads are only half the story. Google Local Services Ads (LSAs) have become the single most important paid channel for home services businesses, and they work differently from traditional pay-per-click.

### How LSAs work for HVAC

LSAs appear above standard Google Ads, above organic results, and above the map pack. They show your company name, review rating, hours, and a "Google Guaranteed" badge that tells homeowners Google has verified your business. According to a [2024 BrightLocal survey](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/), 76% of consumers say they "regularly" read online reviews when choosing a local business, and the Google Guaranteed badge adds an extra layer of trust beyond reviews alone.

The pricing model is what makes LSAs especially valuable: you pay per lead, not per click. A homeowner has to call you or message you through the platform before you're charged. Google's dispute process also lets you contest invalid leads (wrong number, outside your area, spam), which means you're paying almost exclusively for real opportunities.

For most HVAC markets, LSA fees run about $25 to $75 per inquiry. You pay when someone calls or messages, which is still an inquiry. The share of those inquiries that become booked jobs is your close rate, and this page does not have a source for it.

### Standard Google Ads still matter

LSAs don't cover every scenario. If you want to promote maintenance plans, equipment installations, or specific seasonal offers, standard search campaigns give you that flexibility. You can write custom ad copy, send traffic to specific landing pages, and control your messaging in ways LSAs don't allow.

HVAC keywords are expensive. [WordStream's 2024 search benchmarks](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2024/06/04/google-ads-benchmarks) put average cost per click for HVAC terms around $15 to $40. Emergency queries can run higher in competitive metros. That is a cost per click, not a cost per booked job. WordStream's 2026 Facebook report is a different sample and a different channel. It is not a replacement for this search figure.

### How to run search for HVAC

The HVAC companies that get the best return from Google Ads follow a few consistent patterns:

*   **Segment campaigns by service type.** Keep AC repair, furnace installation, and duct cleaning in separate campaigns. Margins and click prices differ, so the budget should too.

*   **Use call tracking.** A unique number per campaign shows which keywords produced a call. A call is an inquiry until it is on the schedule.

*   **Schedule bids around urgency.** Increase bids during evenings and weekends when emergency calls spike and competition for those time slots thins out.

*   **Add location and call assets.** Show the address, phone number, and service area in the ad so the inquiry can start from the result.

*   **Bid on competitor names.** When someone searches "Smith Heating and Air reviews," your ad can appear above their results. It's aggressive, but legal and effective for capturing homeowners who are still comparing options.

**Cost expectation:** $1,500 to $5,000 per month is a planning range for combined LSA and search spend. It is media budget, not a count of booked jobs. Companies in major metros may spend more.

**Best for:** Inquiries from homeowners who are already searching.

Google Ads capture demand that already exists. Meta advertising (Facebook and Instagram) creates demand by reaching homeowners before they have a problem.

Think about it from the homeowner's perspective. Nobody wakes up thinking about their HVAC system, until it breaks. By the time they're searching "AC repair," they're in crisis mode and price sensitivity goes through the roof. Meta ads let you reach those same homeowners weeks or months earlier, when they will still listen to a maintenance plan or an upgrade offer.

### Why Meta works for HVAC

Facebook's targeting options are extremely granular for local home services. You can target by zip code, household income, homeownership status, home age, and even life events like "recently moved." New homeowners often need inspections, maintenance contracts, or system replacements.

On Facebook, the unit cost to use as a reference is a lead in the Home and Home Improvement row of [WordStream's 2026 benchmarks](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/facebook-ads-benchmarks-2026): a median $2.18 per click and $42.95 per lead on leads campaigns, from a sample of at least four U.S. campaigns in that category between April 1, 2025, and June 30, 2026. HVAC is not its own row. A lead in that study is an inquiry, not a booked service call. Meta's company-wide ad revenue is a different number and is covered on [Facebook ad costs](https://adwave.com/resources/facebook-ad-costs/).

### What performs best

The Meta posts that get HVAC inquiries read like a technician talking to a neighbor:

*   **Seasonal maintenance reminders.** "Your AC worked hard this summer. Here's what happens if you skip fall maintenance." These posts ask for the maintenance visit while the homeowner is not in an emergency.

*   **Before-and-after content.** Photos or short videos showing filthy air filters, corroded coils, or dramatic temperature readings before and after service. This type of content stops the scroll because the mess is obvious on a phone screen. [Sprout Social's 2024 benchmarks](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/social-media-benchmarks/) show short-form video gets 2.5 times more engagement than static images on Meta platforms.

*   **Customer testimonial videos.** A 30-second clip of a happy homeowner saying "They came out at 10 p.m. and had our heat running by midnight" carries more weight than any ad copy you'll ever write.

*   **Limited-time offers.** "$49 furnace tune-up before December 1" with a clear call-to-action button that links to your scheduling page.

### Retargeting is where Meta really shines

Someone visited your "AC installation" page and did not request an estimate. You can show them a follow-up ad on Facebook and Instagram. That second impression is still an inquiry path. This page does not cite a close-rate multiple for retargeting versus a first view.

You can also build lookalike audiences from your existing customer list. Upload your customer emails, and Meta's algorithm finds homeowners in your area who share similar demographics and behavior patterns. It's like cloning your best customers.

results.title: Call tracking for small business ads
results.markdown:
Title: Call tracking for small business ads

URL Source: https://adwave.com/resources/call-tracking-for-small-business

Published Time: 2026-10-23T00:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
Call tracking for small business ads gives each ad source its own phone number that forwards to your main line and logs which number was dialed, so you can see whether a call came from TV, search or social.

Website visitors see a number swapped in by a script (dynamic number insertion), and offline ads like TV spots get a fixed number of their own.

Call tracking is software that assigns unique phone numbers to your campaigns, channels or keywords. When someone dials one of those numbers, the software records where the call came from and what happened on it. In [CallRail’s definition of call tracking software](https://www.callrail.com/blog/best-call-tracking-software), the payoff is seeing which marketing produces phone leads as well as which produces clicks. Most tools also keep a recording and a log of the caller’s earlier calls.

Calls drop out of ad reports for a mechanical reason. A click or a form fill happens on a website, where an analytics tag can see it and note the referring ad. A phone call has no such tag attached to it unless you add call tracking yourself. For service businesses like plumbers, dentists, law offices and auto shops, the call is often the conversion that matters. A report built only on form fills undercounts those campaigns and can push budget toward the channel that happens to get more forms.

Business size changes very little about how the setup works. A one-van contractor and a regional chain use the same tracking numbers. The bigger company mostly has more complicated call routing, such as different departments or locations. If you want the basics of logging calls before you think about ad sources, our [step-by-step guide to tracking phone calls](https://adwave.com/resources/how-to-track-phone-calls) covers that ground.

## How tracking numbers and dynamic number insertion work

A tracking number is a forwarding number. It appears in an ad, a customer dials it, and the call rings through to your normal business line. The caller doesn’t notice the forwarding step. Meanwhile the platform logs which tracking number was dialed, and so which ad, along with the caller ID details and a recording. It also notes the call length and whether it connected. A business running search ads and a direct mail piece might buy two numbers, one for each. A week later it can compare how many calls each one produced and listen to what those callers asked.

![Image 1: Woman on a phone call in her kitchen with a laptop open on the counter](https://media.wavefront.adwave-apps.com/ws/ws_adwave/3aa161f0099ced188c5f361de55edfaf4e745a18d319b62773e307b48f028696.jpg)

Fixed numbers work for a print ad or a TV spot because everyone who sees that ad sees the same number, but a website is different because visitors arrive from many places. Dynamic number insertion (DNI) handles that. In practice you install a line of JavaScript on your site. [CallRail’s explanation of how DNI works](https://www.callrail.com/blog/what-is-dynamic-number-insertion) says the script detects the visitor’s source, sets a cookie on their browser, and then displays a matching phone number. The same visitor keeps seeing that number if they leave and come back later. Someone who clicked a Facebook ad sees one number, and someone who arrived from a Google search ad sees another.

DNI can go further and give each visitor session its own number from a pool. That lets the tool tie a call to a specific visit and keyword. Numbers that aren’t in use go back into the pool, which keeps the total number count down. Twilio also notes this recycling as a way to reduce usage. Pool size matters. If the pool is too small for your traffic, two visitors can be shown the same number at once, and the call gets credited to the wrong source. A provider can tell you how many numbers your visit volume needs.

DNI also leaves your local listings alone. Your main number stays in the page’s HTML, so search engines that read the code still find your real number. Only human visitors see the swapped tracking number.

## Tracking calls from TV spots and QR codes

A viewer dials a TV spot’s number straight from the screen, with no website visit along the way for a DNI script to read, so TV needs a fixed number instead. The fix is a static “offline” number used only in that TV spot or campaign. [CallRail’s guide to call tracking for television ads](https://www.callrail.com/blog/call-tracking-for-television-ads) also suggests pairing the spot with a custom landing page URL and putting the same number on that page. That way calls from people who typed in the URL still count toward the TV campaign. Give each spot its own number if you want to compare them. For example, a 15-second offer spot and a 30-second brand spot running in the same week would each need a separate number.

![Image 2: Man on a living room couch picking up his phone while the television is on](https://media.wavefront.adwave-apps.com/ws/ws_adwave/6eadb1fc342616f1efe90ba639631066013966dd27071ab811346d83791a2956.jpg)

Call the number yourself before the ad airs and confirm it shows up in your tracking dashboard labeled as a TV call. A mistyped forwarding setting is much cheaper to find before the spot runs than after a week of untracked calls.

QR codes need a similar workaround, since a QR code that dials a phone number directly can’t be logged: the scan and the call happen on the viewer’s phone and pass through no server. To track it, the code should open a tagged link or landing page first, and that page shows a tracking number tied to the campaign. [ScanKit’s walkthrough of QR code call tracking](https://scankit.app/en/blog/qr-code-call-tracking) lays out that four-step chain: scan, redirect, number assigned, call logged. A QR code on a TV spot or a van then gives you two separate counts to compare, scans against the calls that followed them.

Calls are only one piece of TV measurement. Our explainer on [how TV ad attribution works for small businesses](https://adwave.com/resources/tv-advertising-attribution-small-business) covers the other signals.

## What call tracking costs a small business

Providers usually charge by tracking number, by minute of calls, or as a monthly package that bundles recording and reporting. Published prices from a few providers give a sense of the range:

*   One provider lists tracking numbers from $0.50 a month each plus per-minute charges, and says a typical small business with three to five numbers spends $30 to $75 a month in usage on top of the plan.
*   Analytic Call Tracking’s small-business guide lists a lower-tier plan at $22 a month.
*   [WhatConverts’ 2026 software roundup](https://www.whatconverts.com/blog/best-call-tracking-software/) lists one full-featured tool starting at $30 a month.

Your bill grows with the number of tracking numbers you keep and the size of any DNI pool, plus call minutes and add-ons like recording, transcription or AI call scoring. A business with one static TV number and a small website pool will pay much less than one tracking every keyword. Check each provider’s current pricing page before you sign up, because these figures change.

Keep this cost separate from your media budget. On Adwave, a daily budget from $30 to $10,000 covers media, ads, and management, with [no subscription](https://adwave.com/pricing/). Call tracking software is a separate tool from a separate provider, and you pay for it separately. See [how Adwave works for small businesses](https://adwave.com/for/small-business).

## Setting up call tracking across TV, search and social

1.   Decide which calls count. A new customer asking for a quote is a lead, and an existing customer checking on an order isn’t. Write the rule down so everyone tags calls the same way.
2.   List every source that can produce a call: TV, Google Search, Facebook and Instagram, web and app ads, plus print, your van and your listings.
3.   Assign a static number to each offline source, starting with each TV campaign.
4.   Install DNI on your website so visitors from search and social ads see a number tied to their source.
5.   Decide how to track calls made directly from search ads. Google Ads can [count calls from ads as conversions](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6095882?hl=en) using a Google forwarding number. It judges lead quality from call duration, or from AI analysis of the recording where recording is available (U.S. and Canada only). For background on the platform, see our [Google Ads basics for small businesses](https://adwave.com/resources/google-ads-for-small-business).
6.   Pick one tracking method per source, so you know which report each call total comes from.
7.   Place a test call to every number and confirm each one lands under the right source.
8.   After launch, tag the outcome of each call (booke

results.title: Towing company advertising: channels and budgets
results.markdown:
Title: Towing company advertising: channels and budgets

URL Source: https://adwave.com/resources/towing-company-advertising

Published Time: 2026-11-08T00:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
Towing company advertising works best when drivers already know your name before a breakdown and find you at the top of search during one. Pair Google Search for urgent tow truck near me searches with local TV, Facebook and Instagram so your company is familiar. With Adwave, that mix starts at $30 a day, with ads made from your website.

## How towing companies get customers

Most towing work starts with a phone call from someone who did not plan to need you. A dead battery in a parking lot, a fender bender on the highway, or a car that won’t start in the driveway. That driver grabs a phone, searches, and calls one of the first numbers that looks local and credible. Speed of answer and a familiar name decide a lot of these calls.

A second stream is scheduled work: moving a non-running car to a repair shop, transporting a vehicle someone bought out of town, or flatbed jobs for classic cars and motorcycles. These customers compare options and read a little more before they call, so a clear website with your services and service area helps.

The third stream is repeat and referral work from body shops, dealerships and property managers, plus past customers who remember you. Advertising doesn’t replace those relationships, but it keeps your name in front of the people who make referrals.

Being findable during the emergency matters, and so does being recognized before it. A driver who has seen your truck on a local TV spot or in an Instagram ad is more likely to call you when your name shows up in a list of search results. That is why towing advertising usually combines a channel that catches urgent searches with channels that build local familiarity.

## Which advertising channels fit a towing business

Search catches people who need help right now. TV and social build the name recognition that makes them pick you. Web and mobile placements repeat the message across the apps and sites people use every day. Running them together from one budget is what [multichannel advertising with Adwave](https://adwave.com/solutions/omnichannel) is built for.

![Image 1: Stranded driver on a phone beside a car with hazard lights as a flatbed tow truck approaches at dusk](https://media.wavefront.adwave-apps.com/ws/ws_adwave/7ac50f11152673f1c04c72cfbd143567c6ea7e143463eb6ce543a2e9855ab8c8.jpg)

| Channel | Job for a towing company | Adwave daily budget threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Google Search | Reach drivers searching for a tow, roadside help or a flatbed nearby | From the $30/day minimum |
| Google (YouTube and Demand Gen) | Video and visual reminders to local drivers | Included in the $30/day mix |
| TV / CTV | Local awareness so your name is familiar before a breakdown | From the $30/day minimum |
| Facebook and Instagram | Local awareness, crew and truck photos, community presence | From the $30/day minimum |
| Reddit | Reach local and car-focused communities | Included; availability depends on budget |
| Mobile web and mobile apps | Frequent reminders across sites and apps in your area | Included in the mix |
| TikTok | Short video for younger local drivers | Opt-in, from about $91/day |

The thresholds above follow [Adwave’s published pricing](https://adwave.com/pricing/), where TikTok has to be turned on and connected to a TikTok account. Your budget, audience, creative, settings and content eligibility decide which channels actually run. If one optional channel can’t run at launch, the rest of the campaign still goes live and Adwave tells you why, according to the [Adwave help FAQ](https://adwave.com/help/faq). You don’t open separate ad accounts: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and Reddit ads run on connected accounts Adwave owns, and Adwave sets up a Google Ads account for your workspace.

If you also run a repair shop or dealership alongside the towing side, the guide to [TV advertising for automotive businesses](https://adwave.com/industries/automotive/auto-dealerships/tv-advertising-automotive) covers that audience in more detail.

Adwave daily budgets run from $30 to $10,000, with no subscription and no contract. One all-in daily budget covers media, ads and management. Here is what different levels open up:

| Daily budget | Channels in reach | 30 active days |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $30 | TV, Google (Search included), Facebook and Instagram, web and mobile | $900 |
| $35 | Adds Reddit | $1,050 |
| $75 (pricing page planning example) | Same mix with more room per channel | $2,250 |
| $91 | TikTok becomes available as an opt-in | $2,730 |

The 30-day totals are planning figures. You can pause before 30 days and you’re charged only for what runs. You review your ads before adding a card, then fund a prepaid wallet when you’re ready to launch, and campaigns pause if the wallet runs dry (auto-refill is optional). Card deposits add the processing fee shown at checkout; ACH deposits have no added fee. New accounts start with an empty wallet, and agency licenses and paid extra creative are priced separately from the daily budget.

Be realistic about what a small budget does in a busy metro. At $30 a day spread across TV, search and social, each channel gets a modest share, and urgent towing searches are competitive. A small operator covering one town can get useful visibility at the minimum. A company competing across a large metro will usually need more per day, or a tighter service area, to show up often enough. For broader context on [what local advertising costs](https://adwave.com/resources/local-advertising-cost-guide-2026) across channels, see our cost guide.

Someone who needs a tow is stressed and scanning fast, so a towing ad has to answer the obvious questions in seconds:

![Image 2: Tow operator in a reflective vest loading a sedan onto a flatbed truck in a parking lot](https://media.wavefront.adwave-apps.com/ws/ws_adwave/bec4e04c4b720fdece21011bb9831abfc2f6f816fd8e8791e6f9c84019650c1e.jpg)

*   A phone number that is large, readable and tappable on mobile
*   The towns, ZIP codes or highways you cover
*   The services you actually offer, such as light-duty towing, flatbed transport, jump starts, lockouts or tire changes
*   Real photos of your trucks and crew, not stock images
*   Hours of service, with 24/7 claims only if someone really answers at 3 a.m.

As a campaign example, a single-truck operator might run a TV spot showing the flatbed loading a sedan with the line, for example, Stuck in Springfield? Call now for flatbed towing and roadside help, followed by the phone number and service area on screen. The same photos become Instagram posts, and the search ad lists the same services and towns. That is an illustration of offer, creative and next step, not a measured result.

Adwave reads your website for offers and photos, then builds image ads, social video and a TV spot you can [preview and refine before launch](https://adwave.com/how-it-works/). You can edit the creative or upload finished ads. Campaign creative is included, and extra creation costs $0.38 per image, $6 per social video, $6 per 15-second TV spot and $12 per 30-second TV spot. For more creative angles, our collection of [TV ad ideas for local service businesses](https://adwave.com/resources/home-services-tv-advertising-guide) applies well to towing.

## Planning around weather and seasonal demand

Towing demand rises when conditions get worse, from the first snow and ice storms to heat waves that kill batteries, heavy rain and busy holiday travel weekends. Search demand follows those events almost immediately, so your search presence needs budget available on those days.

![Image 3: Wrecker truck with amber lights recovering a car from a snowy roadside ditch in early morning](https://media.wavefront.adwave-apps.com/ws/ws_adwave/d1539967c30f4204e97a90a52d4a201eb89dfba7f4e2185bfc8187f8aba95e54.jpg)

Awareness channels work on a slower clock. A TV or social campaign that starts the morning of a storm has little time to make your name familiar. Running awareness steadily, then raising the daily budget a week or two before your known busy season, gives drivers time to see you before they need you. When the season eases, lower the budget rather than going dark entirely.

Budget changes in Adwave are simple to time. On a live campaign, a new daily budget applies the same day if your wallet covers it, with no proration. Pausing stops future daily charges; the day’s set-aside stays until the next morning, when only what ran is charged. Low delivery never pauses a live campaign on its own. A short pause won’t erase your setup, but a long one gives up the familiarity you built.

Target your actual service area with a radius, ZIP codes or a city, so a storm push doesn’t spend money in towns your trucks can’t reach. Tree service companies face the same pattern, and their approach t
